title: The Empire of Hrossagrið
text: Entry I · The founding meaning Why the Empire carries this name Recorded in the imperial register Hrossagrið is not named for its horses. It is named for its grið — guaranteed peace, safe conduct, quarter, sanctuary — and for the horses that define whom the sanctuary is owed to. The name was not chosen. It was given, in the Viking Age, by Norse speakers who found a law that granted horses protected peace ridiculous. They had two words for it. Hrossaþrælar — horse-thralls — was thrown at the people. Hrossagrið mocked what their law did: that place where even a horse receives legal peace . The insult aimed at people died with the quarrel. The one that named a jurisdiction did not: outsiders who had never been in the quarrel heard only a plain description — the country that protects horses — and used it as such. The Hrossagrith knew exactly where it came from and took it anyway. Note in the margin The charge was that these were people who had put an animal under the protection of the law. The Empire has never disputed the charge. See how the name was given . Protection of a person is incomplete where the person’s horse, means of movement, livelihood, or route home may still be seized, abused, exhausted, or used as leverage. title: Horses
text: National treasure Horses Every other part of this portal could be explained without mentioning horses. None of it would exist in this shape without them. The Empire is named for the protection owed to horses, and that protection is the oldest thing in its law. What follows is not sentiment: it is the reasoning by which the Empire decides what may and may not be done to an animal, and the marks by which its road system makes that decision visible. Scope Hrossagrithic law covers ponies, donkeys, mules, hinnies and other equids. The ancient national name keeps the horse only as its representative root. Article I Welfare and bitless control Why ordinary bits are prohibited A bit is an object placed in a horse’s mouth and connected to the reins, so that the rider or driver controls the animal by pressure through the mouth. In most of the horse world this is unremarkable. In Hrossagrið ordinary bits are simply banned, and the reasoning runs through the Fifth Dynamic . Because the horse counts as a life form in its own right rather than as somebody’s property, the analysis cannot end at what is convenient for the rider. The state has to ask what happens to the horse, whether pain is risked, whether a less destructive alternative exists, and whether the animal can be controlled safely without a device in its mouth. Where the answer is yes, human convenience is not enough to justify the additional risk. Approved bitless headgear includes sidepulls, hackamores, bosals, cross-unders and cordeos. What is lawful is set by the Imperial Tack, Restraint and Welfare Code and measured against the Imperial Tack Measurement Schedule; road use adds further requirements on top. Slaughter. Hrossagrithic culture and law treat equids far closer to companion animals and working partners than to food animals. Other societies have long traditions of eating horse meat; the Empire does not regard that as a reason to tolerate an equid-meat industry. Horse slaughter is one of the gravest equid-welfare crimes — and the human offender still receives the highest available non-lethal penalties, because the death penalty is absolutely prohibited . Not a Scientology rule The Eight Dynamics supply the ethical frame. The conclusion — that bits are banned — is a Hrossagrithic political decision drawn from that frame plus the evidence on equine welfare. Article II Road status at a glance The mark every equid carries onto a public road Every equid entering a public road wears approved bitless headgear fitted with a Facial Marker — a marker-bearing frentera or muserola carrying an interchangeable

title: Road-status markers
text: Book III · Standard Public-road equid status marking The final and binding universal standard for every public-road equid. The Carriage Code may impose additional or stricter requirements on top of it. Every equid entering a public road shall wear approved public-road bitless headgear fitted with an approved Facial Marker displaying that equid’s current interchangeable retroreflective and switchably illuminated road-status insert. The marker is a road instruction to humans. It shall not be used as advertisement, as decoration alone, as medical disclosure beyond necessity, as shame marking, or as a replacement for the judgement of the rider or driver. Definitions Frentera and muserola A frentera is a frontal component running vertically down the centre of the face from the upper bridle, headstall, browband or crown area toward the forehead or nasal bridge. It may be narrow, X-shaped, branched, broad or panel-like. A component confined to crossing or encircling the nose, with no upper vertical facial connection, is not a frentera. A muserola is a noseband or nosepiece crossing and ordinarily encircling the nose. It may be broad, decorative, separately mounted, or integrated into a lawful control noseband, and need not attach to the browband or crownpiece. Either qualifies as a Facial Marker only where it provides a dedicated, clearly visible insert field of sufficient size and contrast for road use. A small ornament, medallion, stud or badge that cannot carry the insert visibly does not qualify. No body marking No paint, dye, clipping, branding, glue, mane attachment, tail attachment, skin marking or coat alteration may be used to show status. Ever. Ordinary and restricted markers Colour is never the only distinction White field Ordinary road-certified equid. Green field Green equid, provisional certificate, training status, or supervised road work. Yellow field Caution: sensitivity, extra-space requirement, or heightened startle risk. White field, red border Restricted passing. Pass only on the signal of the driver, rider or handler. Red field, white X Do not pass. Stop and wait: an active hazard or immediate control condition exists. Service markers Issued and verified through authorised channels only Blue, Road Guard emblem Imperial Road Guard, traffic patrol, road-control service. Blue, police shield Police service, where authorised. White, red cross Ambulance or authorised medical emergency service. Red, white flame Fire or rescue service. Green, paw and hoof Veterinary emergency service. Blue, pegasus Imperial post, messenger or courier service. Blac

title: Living in Hrossagrið
text: Book II Living in Hrossagrið What the Empire provides, requires and guarantees for the people who live within its protection. The sections below follow from one principle rather than from a list of policies. The legitimate purpose of state power in Hrossagrið is to make existence as constructive and as little destructive as possible across the whole breadth of life, judged on the best available evidence about what a decision will actually do. Free healthcare, free education and strict child protection are not generosity: they are what that principle produces when it is applied honestly. Where this comes from See the state and its doctrine for eudaimonocracy, the Eight Dynamics and the two Crowns. The register of parts Sections of this book Six parts, each held separately in the register Part I Health Free at the point of use, heavily funded, and designed against waiting lists, staff shortages and regional inequality. Part II Education & children Free education at every level, free childcare regardless of parental employment, and exceptionally strong protection for children. Part III Transport & roads Horse-drawn road transport, rail, and the single narrow motor-freight exception known as Hrossaway. Part IV Justice & policing Police selection and training on an aviation model, de-escalation by default, and an absolute prohibition of the death penalty. Part V Work & money Progressive taxation of income, wealth, capital gains and large inheritances. Part VI Citizenship & refuge A diverse human nation descended from many peoples integrated over centuries through migration and refuge.

title: Health
text: Book II · Part I Health Free at the point of use, heavily funded, and deliberately designed against the failures that make free healthcare fail elsewhere. Healthcare in Hrossagrið is free at the point of use. That much is easy to declare and hard to deliver, so the design goal is stated in the negative: the system is built to prevent waiting lists, staff shortages and regional inequality, rather than to announce a right and then ration it quietly. Evidence before intention Why the Empire re-tests what it already believes Ethics decides what counts as constructive; science establishes what is actually happening. A treatment is not adopted because its purpose is good. It is adopted because research, replication, statistics, monitoring of adverse effects and comparison with alternatives say it works. If a drug does not work, good intentions do not license its use. The same rule applies backwards in time. New research is not automatically better than old research, and an excellent old study that survives modern testing stays. But an old claim earns no permanent immunity from having sat in textbooks for a century. Old medical dogmas, psychological theories and professional standards are asked the same question: was this ever properly tested? Women and children Where the historical record is weakest Much of medical literature was produced in societies with severe sexism and very different attitudes to children. Where the older evidence studied women poorly, the Empire does not treat that as unfortunate but final. It deliberately funds research into women’s pain, gynaecological disease, cardiovascular disease in women, drug effects in women, autism and other conditions in girls, and maternal health. A child is not treated as a smaller adult. Research has to account for a developing body and mind, and clinical practice follows the research rather than tradition. In preparation. The organisation of imperial hospitals, veterinary-adjacent services, ambulance provision and the medical professions is not yet written into the register. The Imperial Emergency Medical Carriage Technical Standard, which governs ambulance carriages, is in force . Related Imperial Emergency Medical Carriage Technical Standard — ambulance speed, low jostle, suspension, emergency lanes and testing. Principle Ethics says what matters. Science says what is true. Neither substitutes for the other.

title: Education and children
text: Book II · Part II Education and children Free at every level, genuinely accessible, and paired with the strongest protective duties the Empire imposes anywhere in its law. Education in Hrossagrið is free, heavily funded and genuinely accessible at every level — the last word doing real work, since a fee-free system that is unreachable in practice is not accessible at all. Historical education The Empire does not teach a flattering version of itself Historical education is accurate about the Empire’s successes, failures, injustices, conflicts and controversial decisions. Material written for younger children may omit graphic detail, but it may not falsify what occurred, and greater detail is introduced progressively with age. The Empire does not rewrite, erase or sanitise its history for political purposes. Childcare Free or effectively free, and not conditional on employment Childcare is free or effectively free, plentiful, properly staffed and heavily funded. It is available regardless of whether the parents are employed — a deliberate refusal to treat childcare as a subsidy attached to work rather than as provision for the child. Protection of children Duties, not aspirations Children receive exceptionally strong protection from violence, exploitation, neglect, institutional abuse and coercive control, and they must be heard in decisions affecting them. Alongside enforcement, the Empire runs free and aggressively advertised public programmes teaching parenting, emotional regulation, respectful conflict, children’s rights, and how to recognise and break generational cycles of abuse. These are easy to join and presented as ordinary public education — not as therapy, and not as punishment for bad people. In preparation. The structure of imperial schooling, examinations, teacher training and higher education is not yet written into the register. Foundational values Historical honesty · meritocracy · animal welfare · scientific progress · environmental stewardship · refugee integration · social equality · ethical governance.

title: Transport and roads
text: Book II · Part III Transport and roads A country whose road culture is built on equids, and the one narrow exception it makes for motor freight. Hrossagrið fundamentally does not want ordinary motor roads. Its public roads are built around ridden and driven equids, and every animal entering one carries a road-status marker declaring what other road users must do about it. Hrossaway The exception, and why it exists The Empire also exists in the real world. It needs imports, exports, medicine, industrial equipment, raw materials and international trade. It could refuse all motor freight on principle — and then damage its economy, complicate the supply of medical equipment, and create a great deal of new harm. That would be a strange outcome for a system whose whole purpose is to minimise destruction. Hrossaway is the resulting narrow exception: a closed motor-freight road running from an international port or border freight point to a specific transfer terminal. A truck enters. It unloads. From there goods continue by rail or by heavy horse-drawn freight teams. The principle is not abandoned, and it is also not turned into a suicidal dogma. Carriages and emergency transport Where the binding detail lives Carriage work is governed in full by the Imperial Code for the Welfare of Working Carriage Equids: passports, certification, workload and rest, weather burden, route safety, harness, headgear mounts, road-status inserts, lighting and ground-guidance lamps. Ambulance carriages have their own technical standard covering speed, low jostle, suspension, emergency lanes and glideways. In preparation. Road authority and infrastructure law — construction, maintenance and control of the public road network — is reserved for separate drafting so that carriage welfare law does not absorb it. Rail and the wider public-infrastructure system are not yet written into the register. On the roads Every equid on a public road wears approved bitless headgear with a Facial Marker. See the full marker standard

title: Justice and policing
text: Book II · Part IV Justice and policing Selection and training on an aviation model, de-escalation as the default, and penalties for officials harsher than for the citizens they police. Police recruitment and training in Hrossagrið are comparable to aviation: strict selection, long practical training, simulations, recurring examinations, psychological assessment and mandatory recertification. The comparison is deliberate. A profession that can kill people by error is trained like one. Conduct and accountability The asymmetry is intentional De-escalation is the default. Any unnecessary violence, dishonesty, evidence manipulation, discriminatory conduct or abuse of authority brings independent investigation and penalties harsher than those imposed on an ordinary citizen abusing the same power. The death penalty Prohibited absolutely, without exception Modern law prohibits the human death penalty absolutely — including for treason, corruption, animal cruelty, horse slaughter and emergency offences. Hrossagrið has never established ordinary judicial execution as a legitimate civilian punishment, though executions may have occurred during civil war or historical crises as unlawful killings or atrocities. History records them honestly rather than quietly. The gravest equid-welfare crimes therefore carry the highest available non-lethal penalties: potentially life imprisonment, permanent disqualification from public office and animal custody, forfeiture, restitution, and corporate dissolution where applicable. Consent Defined by consent, applied without exemption Rape law is consent-based and applies equally within marriage and relationships. Coercion, intoxication, incapacity and abuse of authority invalidate consent. Police, forensic staff, prosecutors and judges handling these cases require specialist certification. Privacy, surveillance and cybercrime Severe penalties, and one deliberately severe exception Privacy violations and cybercrime carry exceptionally severe penalties — especially surveillance, stalking, doxxing, identity theft, intimate-image abuse, database trafficking and attacks on essential infrastructure. Public infrastructure is extensively monitored by camera, but footage is encrypted, access-logged, time-limited and usable only for legally defined purposes; facial recognition and personal tracking require exceptional legal authorisation, and misuse by an official is itself a serious privacy offence. Against that, the Empire operates a deliberately exceptional regime for dark-web access. Reliably attributed access to hidden services automatic

title: Work and money
text: Book II · Part V Work and money Progressive taxation, serious treatment of avoidance, and one prohibition that surprises visitors. Income, wealth, capital gains and large inheritances are progressively taxed. Aggressive tax avoidance and the hiding of wealth abroad are serious offences rather than clever arrangements, and they are treated as such. Artificial intelligence A prohibition rather than a policy preference AI data centres are prohibited within Hrossagrið. Foreign AI services may be accessed only under strict privacy, energy, copyright and national-security rules. In preparation. Employment law, wages, pensions, industrial organisation, currency and the imperial budget process are not yet written into the register. The constitutional continuity budget — what happens to public money when the two Crowns deadlock — is described under government . Meritocracy One of the eight foundational values. Registers and professional rosters are maintained by permanent civil servants under published objective qualifications; applicants cannot be excluded for political loyalty or personal favour.

title: Citizenship and refuge
text: Book II · Part VI Citizenship and refuge The Empire is named for sanctuary. Its population is what centuries of sanctuary produced. Modern Hrossagrið is a highly diverse human nation whose population descends from numerous peoples integrated over centuries through migration and refuge. Refugee integration is one of the eight foundational values of the state, and it is not a recent addition: it is the oldest thing the country was known for. The name itself records the practice. Neighbouring merchants, messengers, diplomats, refugees, riders and handlers used hrossagrið for the legal protection encountered at the border. Once a person crossed into the territory, foreign pursuit had to stop. The traveller, their companions and their equids entered protection together, because protection that stops at the animal is not protection at all. Usage How the demonym works The citizen term is Hrossagrith , and it is invariant: it takes no singular or plural suffix. The correct singular usage is I am Hrossagrith ; the correct collective usage is the Hrossagrith people . The adjective and cultural term is Hrossagrithic . In preparation. Naturalisation procedure, residence, asylum determination and travel documents are not yet written into the register. For the historical practice from which they descend, see the early history . A human state Citizens, monarchs, officials, voters, workers, patients and passengers are people. Equids are protected living beings and working partners; they are not the population and hold no human political office.

title: Government
text: Book I The state and its doctrine The full constitutional description of Hrossagrið is a eudaimonocratic diarchic monarchy. Eudaimonocracy answers why state power exists. The diarchy answers who holds it. A human state. Hrossagrið is governed by and for humans. Its citizens, monarchs, officials, voters, workers, patients and passengers are people. Horses and other equids are protected living beings and working partners; they are not the population and hold no human political office. Eudaimonocracy Article I · The purpose of state power The name comes from eudaimonia , the classical Greek idea usually mistranslated as happiness. It is closer to flourishing : a life going well as a whole, rather than a moment that feels good. A person can enjoy something while destroying their own life, and something unpleasant today can be necessary for a genuinely good life overall. From that comes the Hrossagrithic term: government oriented toward flourishing. But the Empire does not simply copy Aristotle. Classical eudaimonia is primarily about human flourishing, and Hrossagrið deliberately widens the frame using an existing eight-part ethical scheme. The legitimate purpose of state power is to maximise constructive survival and flourishing and minimise serious destruction across the Eight Dynamics, using the best available evidence to determine the real consequences of policy. The Eight Dynamics Article II · The ethical frame, and where it comes from The Eight Dynamics are not a Hrossagrithic invention. They are a concept from Scientology, which describes the basic principle of existence as a drive toward survival divided into eight interconnected urges. The Empire borrows that framework as its ethical scheme; the political conclusions drawn from it are its own. Self — the urge to survive as an individual and to be oneself. Creativity — making things for the future: sex, family, children, raising them, creation directed forward. Groups — survival through or as a group of any scale, from a school class to a state. Mankind — the human species as a whole, distinct from any one nation. Life Forms — animals, birds, insects, fish and vegetation; life itself. Physical Universe — matter, energy, space and time. Spiritual Dynamic — spiritual beings, spiritual existence, and the spiritual source of life. Infinity — existence as infinity, associated with God, the Supreme Being or the Creator. title: Imperial law
text: Book III The imperial legal corpus Codes in force, the technical standards that carry their measurable detail, the official templates they create, and the law still reserved for drafting. Because the state name itself remembers protected passage, equid welfare is not decorative symbolism. It follows directly from the Fifth Dynamic and sits near the centre of imperial law. Protecting a person while allowing their horse or other equid to be abused, seized, overworked or used as leverage is not true protection, and every instrument below is read against that principle. Reading order A code states obligations and offences. A standard carries the measurable detail and is amended more often. A template is a form whose layout is fixed by the instrument that creates it. Codes in force Binding law In force · General code General Imperial Equid Welfare Code The principal welfare instrument of the Empire, covering equids in every setting rather than one line of work. In force · Sectoral code Imperial Code for the Welfare of Working Carriage Equids Carriage welfare in full: passports, certification, workload and rest, weather burden, route safety, harness, headgear mounts, road-status inserts, lighting, ground-guidance lamps, emergency medical carriages, enforcement, offences and interim schedules. In force · Sectoral code Imperial Tack, Restraint, and Welfare Code Equipment placed on the animal, and the limits on restraint. The Empire’s bitless-only welfare principle is stated here. In force · Sectoral code Imperial Road and Driver Code Conduct on public roads and the duties of drivers, with the universal requirement that every equid entering a public road displays its road status. In force · Sectoral code Imperial Mounted Service and Road Patrol Code Binding law for mounted police, the mounted Road Guard, ridden couriers and patrol equids — ridden service, which is not carriage work and is governed separately. In force · Sectoral code Imperial Breeding and Registry Code Breeding practice and the imperial registry. Technical standards Thresholds, dimensions, colours and testing In force · Standard Imperial Public-Road Equid Status Marking Standard The universal marking rule for every equid on a public road. Status is shown by an interchangeable insert held in a marker-bearing frentera or muserola, road-grade retroreflective and self-illuminating in its assigned colour. No paint, dye, clipping, branding, glue or coat alteration is permitted. title: History
text: Book IV Early history Four reconstructed parts covering c. 1200–100 BC. The account does not begin with a desired modern territory, and it does not grant the Empire a national birth the evidence cannot carry. Historical method. This reconstruction combines real archaeological constraints with a fictional Hrossagrith tradition. Archaeology can constrain environments, technologies, settlement patterns and material exchange; it cannot verify the particular feuds, decisions, speeches or motives recorded here. Where the surviving tradition cannot distinguish among several explanations, the account preserves that uncertainty rather than presenting one motive as established fact. Skip to a part Part I · c. 1200–650 BC — before the people, and the crisis Part II · c. 650–500 BC — the unreliable network Part III · c. 500–300 BC — renewal, over-reach, first political horses Part IV · c. 300–100 BC — speed, and what it could not buy Expand all parts c. 1200–650 BC Part I Before the people, and the crisis that made them c. 1200–1050 BC Before the Hrossagrith people There is no Hrossagrith people, state or common identity. The central Irish lowlands hold scattered farming communities around the middle Shannon, Lough Ree, central Westmeath, eastern Roscommon and northern Offaly. Authority belongs to households, kin groups and local leaders rather than permanent states. Horses may be present in small numbers, but they are not yet the basis of society, law or government — and the region that later becomes the Hrossagrith core is one ordinary inland area among several wealthier ones. Territorial status: no Compact, no shared territory. c. 1050–980 BC The Crossing Crisis The first lasting divergence is placed at an important crossing on the middle Shannon — already more than a practical route, used for seasonal exchange, marriage arrangements, ritual gatherings, dispute settlement and the movement of livestock and travellers. A succession of disputes over stolen cattle, access to the crossing and old killings widens into a feud. Retaliation spreads beyond the original families; travellers are attacked, repairs stop, and the crossing becomes unusable. Everyone nearby suffers: livestock cannot be moved safely, traders avoid the route, isolated settlements become vulnerable. Across several later gatherings, influential households repeatedly restore and extend a temporary peace custom — approximately, a prohibition on killing or seizing an accepted participant during a gathering or on its recognised approaches. title: Name and symbols
text: Book V Name, etymology and national symbol The state name is formed from two genuine Old Norse elements by a genuine Old Norse compound pattern. What follows is the canonical explanation for legal, educational, diplomatic and cultural use. Canonical forms Article I · How the name is written Official native name: Hrossagrið International spelling: Hrossagrith Formal state name: The Empire of Hrossagrið Citizen / demonym: Hrossagrith , invariant — no singular or plural suffix Adjective and cultural term: Hrossagrithic Practical English pronunciation: HROSS-a-grith The correct singular usage is I am Hrossagrith ; the correct collective usage is the Hrossagrith people . Use the international th -based forms wherever ð is unavailable or difficult to type. Core meaning Article II · What the name says Hrossagrið means horse-sanctuary, horse-protection, or protected peace for horses and the people bound to them. The central idea is grið : sanctuary, guaranteed protection, safe conduct, legal immunity, protected peace, and the stopping of pursuit or retaliation. The name is not meant to say that the country is merely the horse country. It means a place where sanctuary is real enough that a traveller is protected together with the living bond that carries them. Etymology Article III · The compound and its two elements The name consists of hross + -a + grið — more precisely, of the genitive-plural compound form hrossa- and the noun grið . The internal -a is not decorative and not an English linking vowel: it is the genitive plural ending of hross , giving the first element the meaning “of horses”. Old Norse compounds are understood from the final element backward. The head is grið : the name is a form, place or jurisdiction of protection, specified by horses — not a horse modified by peace. The first element: hross Old Norse hross is a neuter noun meaning horse — an ordinary historical horse-word, not a poetic invention. Its genitive plural is hrossa , and because the uninflected singular and plural can both appear as hross , that form matters: it makes the collective relation explicit. The name does not mean one horse’s protection. It invokes horses collectively. It belongs to an old Germanic family: Old English hors , Old Saxon hros , Old High German hros or ros , German Ross , Icelandic hross . A commonly proposed deeper reconstruction is Proto-Germanic *hrussą , sometimes connected with an older idea of running, but that derivation is not certain enough to be treated as the official meaning. The secure meaning is the attested one: horse. The second element: gri

title: About
text: Colophon About this portal Hrossagrith is a fictional country, and this site is the reference portal for it. Hrossagrith does not exist. It is an invented country. This site is a worldbuilding project and has no connection to any real state, government, ministry, agency or official body, and it does not represent or claim to represent any such organisation. Nothing published here is a real law, a real regulation or a real government notice, and none of it should be relied upon as one. Method Two habits that shape everything here The first is that uncertainty is preserved rather than resolved . Where the invented tradition cannot distinguish among several explanations, the text says so instead of choosing one and presenting it as settled. Where the deeper prehistory of a word is genuinely disputed, it is marked as disputed rather than converted into fact. The second is that real constraints are respected where they apply . The linguistic analysis uses attested Old Norse morphology; the historical reconstruction works within what is plausible for Iron Age Ireland rather than against it. The invented parts are the feuds, decisions and institutions — not the grammar, and not the archaeology. Borrowed frameworks Stated openly rather than disguised The Empire’s political doctrine uses the Eight Dynamics , a concept belonging to Scientology, as its ethical framework. That borrowing is named on the government page . It is not an endorsement, an affiliation, or a claim to represent Scientology, and no text from Scientology’s own materials is reproduced here — the Dynamics are summarised in this project’s own words. Every political conclusion drawn from them is fictional and Hrossagrithic. The classical concept of eudaimonia is likewise drawn from Aristotelian ethics and adapted rather than reproduced. Illustration Where the pictures come from The flag is the author’s own. Every other image on this portal — the state mark, the section icons, the ornaments and rules, the road-status marker drawings and the banner illustration — is original vector artwork drawn for this site. No third-party photographs or stock images are used anywhere. Status Under construction, and saying so Sections are published as they are written, and full texts of the imperial instruments will be added one at a time. Where a section of national life has not yet been written into the canon, this portal marks it in preparation rather than inventing an answer.
